title: Add WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata pointer to invalid/expired token 401
description:

Impact: a client (e.g. Spark's OpenAuth library) presenting an expired JWT gets a bare 401. Without the resource_metadata pointer it cannot re-initiate RFC 9728 discovery automatically — it has no hint about where to go. The missing-token path is correct; the invalid-token path is inconsistent.

title: Add logMCPMethod middleware to make MCP message types visible in logs
description:

Body is reconstructed via io.MultiReader so the downstream handler sees nothing missing.

eldamo-server currently has sseLoggingMiddleware (main.go:291-300) which only logs '[HTTP Request] POST /sse from …'. Every MCP protocol message — initialize, tools/list, tools/call, notifications — is indistinguishable in Cloud Run logs. This made debugging the Spark session (13 tool calls over 10 minutes) require correlating raw timestamps rather than reading intent from log lines.

title: P2: Implement RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration (coexisting with CIMD)
description:
Add RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration so 'automatic registration' works for Gemini Spark. This is what removes the visible error 'This server does not support automatic registration. To connect, enter your own OAuth client ID and secret below.' DCR and CIMD are two interchangeable ways for a client to obtain a client_id; both terminate in the SAME authorization_code + PKCE core already implemented (handleTokenExchange, oauth.go:441, which already accepts arbitrary client_id + code_verifier).

WHY: The server advertises only CIMD (client_id_metadata_document_supported: true, main.go:369) and exposes no registration_endpoint. Spark speaks DCR, not the newer CIMD draft, so it sees no automatic registration mechanism it understands and falls back to the manual client-id/secret prompt (which also won't work today because the token endpoint is built for public clients: token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported ['none']).

WHAT TO DO:
1. Implement POST /api/oauth/register (RFC 7591). Accept client metadata (redirect_uris [required], client_name, grant_types, response_types, token_endpoint_auth_method, scope). Since this is a public/PKCE server, register clients as PUBLIC: issue an opaque client_id, NO client_secret (token_endpoint_auth_method 'none'). Return the standard RFC 7591 registration response (client_id, client_id_issued_at, redirect_uris, etc.).
2. Validate/whitelist redirect_uris. Follow RFC 8252 loopback port-agnostic matching (per AGENTS.md CIMD compliance note) so native/loopback clients work.
3. Persist registered clients (client_id -> redirect_uris + metadata) in Firestore, in the mithlond-services database instance (NOT default), consistent with existing storage. Reuse the same validated shape already used for CIMD docs (oauth.go:165-227 fetchClientMetadata redirect_uris handling). Consider a dedicated collection (e.g. registered_clients) with optional TTL if desired.
4. Advertise registration_endpoint in the RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata (handleOAuthDiscovery, main.go:365-374). KEEP client_id_metadata_document_supported: true — DCR and CIMD must coexist; advertise both and let the client choose.
5. Wire the authorize/token flow to accept DCR-issued client_ids: handleAuthCallback (oauth.go:272) and handleTokenExchange (oauth.go:441) currently resolve client identity via CIMD URL fetch. Add a branch that resolves a locally-registered client_id from Firestore (vs. fetching a CIMD URL when client_id is an https URL). PKCE verification (oauth.go:539-546) and JWT issuance are unchanged.
6. Ensure the issued HMAC JWT is identical regardless of onboarding path, and works for BOTH /sse and /a2a ('one token, both protocols').
7. Mount /api/oauth/register on the existing mux; note the frontend (mithlond-web) proxies /api/oauth/** via Hosting rewrite — confirm the new path is covered by that proxy so CORS is avoided.

ACCEPTANCE:
- POST /api/oauth/register with a valid redirect_uris returns 201 with a client_id and no secret.
- The full authorization_code + PKCE flow completes end-to-end using a DCR-issued client_id and yields a working JWT accepted at /sse and /a2a.
- Existing CIMD (client-id-as-URL) clients continue to work unchanged (regression covered).
- Auth-server metadata advertises BOTH registration_endpoint and client_id_metadata_document_supported: true.
- Unit tests: register endpoint validation (missing redirect_uris rejected), DCR client_id resolution branch, and coexistence with CIMD.
- Manual verify: Gemini Spark completes 'automatic registration' against candir.mithlond.com/sse without manual client-id/secret entry.

DEPENDS ON P1 (RFC 9728) — Spark must be able to discover the auth server before registration is exercised end-to-end.

SECURITY: Log rejection reasons via log.Printf to Cloud Run stderr (AGENTS.md). All external fetches through SafeHTTPClient(). Keep signature-only stateless JWT validation during tool execution.
notes:
Implemented RFC 7591 DCR coexisting with CIMD (oauth.go + main.go):
- New POST /api/oauth/register (handleClientRegistration): open registration for PUBLIC/PKCE clients. Issues opaque client_id (prefix 'mcp-client-'), NO client_secret, token_endpoint_auth_method 'none'. Persists to Firestore collection 'registered_clients' in mithlond-services DB (reuses firestoreClient; no new IAM needed).
- buildClientRegistration(): pure/testable validation — redirect_uris required, max 10, each must be https or http-on-loopback (RFC 8252); rejects non-'none' auth methods; applies default grant/response types.
- resolveClient(ctx, clientID): dispatches by client_id shape — URL -> FetchAndValidateCIMD (unchanged CIMD path); opaque -> getRegisteredClient (Firestore). handleAuthCallback now calls resolveClient instead of FetchAndValidateCIMD. Token exchange (handleTokenExchange) needed NO change — it already matches stored client_id + verifies PKCE and issues the same JWT.
- handleOAuthDiscovery now advertises registration_endpoint AND keeps client_id_metadata_document_supported:true (both front doors).
- Mounted /api/oauth/register on mux (covered by mithlond-web /api/oauth/** Hosting rewrite).
- Tests: oauth_dcr_test.go (build validation cases, handler 201/400/405, no client_secret, client_id dispatch) + discovery test asserts registration_endpoint & CIMD coexistence. Full suite green, golangci-lint 0 issues. Local curl verified discovery + 400/405 + Firestore write attempt.

FOLLOW-UP / VERIFY (sibling repo mithlond-web): the /mcp-auth SPA must forward a NON-URL client_id (DCR-issued) unchanged to /api/oauth/authorize-callback. If the SPA assumes client_id is a URL or validates it as one, Spark's end-to-end will break at the consent step even though the backend accepts it. Needs a check/possibly a small SPA change before declaring Spark fully working end-to-end.

Not committed (conservative default; other agent committing unrelated files).

title: P1: Implement RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata + WWW-Authenticate pointer
description:
Add RFC 9728 (OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata) discovery so modern MCP clients (Spark, opencode) can discover the authorization server. This is the root defect behind the Cloud Logging 404 storm and affects ALL modern clients, not just Spark. Purely additive; breaks no existing CIMD/OAuth 2.1 client.

WHY: The current MCP authorization spec requires the resource server to publish Protected Resource Metadata. Clients probe the well-known path (with the resource path inserted per RFC 9728) BEFORE they ever reach the RFC 8414 authorization-server document the server already serves at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (main.go:466). Without PRM, discovery dead-ends at 404.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Add a handler that serves the Protected Resource Metadata JSON document containing at minimum: resource (the canonical resource identifier / base URL), authorization_servers (array containing the base URL that serves /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server), scopes_supported (e.g. ['lexicon:read'] to match gate() in main.go:456), bearer_methods_supported (['header']). Derive scheme://host from the request honoring X-Forwarded-Host exactly as handleOAuthDiscovery does (main.go:350-362) / requestBaseURL.
2. Mount at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource AND the path-suffixed variants the clients probe first: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/sse and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/a2a (RFC 9728 clients insert the resource path). Confirmed in logs: GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/sse -> 404 then GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource -> 404.
3. Keep these endpoints PUBLIC/unauthenticated (per AGENTS.md 'public discovery, protected protocol'), mounted on the existing http.ServeMux in main() alongside the other well-known handlers.
4. Add the resource_metadata pointer to the 401 challenge in oauthMiddleware (oauth.go:685): WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Mithlond", error="unauthorized", resource_metadata="<baseURL>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource". Build the absolute URL from the request base.
5. Since both /sse and /a2a sit behind the same oauthMiddleware, ensure the PRM document/pointer covers both resources (single shared PRM doc referencing the same authorization server is acceptable; keep auth unified per 'one token, both protocols').

ACCEPTANCE:
- GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource returns 200 with valid RFC 9728 JSON (issuer/authorization_servers resolvable to the RFC 8414 doc).
- GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/sse returns 200 (or a documented redirect) rather than 404.
- A 401 from /sse and /a2a includes a WWW-Authenticate header with a resource_metadata parameter pointing to the PRM doc.
- Unit tests mirroring main_test.go TestOAuthDiscovery (GET returns metadata, non-GET rejected) added for the new endpoints.
- Manual verify: opencode and Spark discovery proceed past the 404 stage.

NON-GOALS: DCR (P2) and transport shape (P3) are separate tasks.
notes:
Implemented in main.go + oauth.go:
- Added handleProtectedResourceMetadata (main.go) serving RFC 9728 PRM. Public/unauthenticated, CORS-enabled, GET+OPTIONS only. Derives resource id from path suffix so /sse and /a2a variants report resource=baseURL/sse and /a2a; bare path reports baseURL. authorization_servers=[baseURL] (this host's RFC 8414 doc), scopes_supported=[lexicon:read], bearer_methods_supported=[header]. Uses requestBaseURL(r) (honors X-Forwarded-Host).
- Mounted at protectedResourceMetadataPrefix and prefix+'/' (subtree) in main() mux, next to the RFC 8414 endpoint.
- oauth.go 401 challenge now includes RFC 9728 resource_metadata="<baseURL>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" pointer.
- Tests: TestProtectedResourceMetadata (bare, /sse suffix, 405 non-GET, 204 OPTIONS+CORS) and TestUnauthorizedChallengePointsToPRM. Full suite green, golangci-lint 0 issues.
- Manual curl verified on PORT=8099: PRM bare/sse/a2a all 200 with correct resource; 401 on /sse carries resource_metadata; RFC 8414 doc unchanged.
Not committed (conservative default).

title: [EPIC] Broaden OAuth client onboarding: RFC 9728 + RFC 7591 for Gemini Spark & general MCP clients
description:
Gemini Spark (and other modern MCP clients such as opencode) cannot connect to the deployed candir/eldamo MCP+A2A server. Two independent gaps, surfaced by Cloud Logging 404s on testingproject-19c4c/eldamo-mcp-server:

1) The server does not publish RFC 9728 OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata. Clients probe GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/sse and get 404, so discovery of the authorization server never completes. This affects ALL modern MCP clients (opencode fails identically), not just Spark. The current MCP authorization spec requires the resource server to publish this document.

2) The server offers only CIMD (client_id_metadata_document_supported: true, client-id-as-URL) as a client-onboarding mechanism and does not implement RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration (no registration_endpoint). Spark speaks DCR, not CIMD, so it reports 'This server does not support automatic registration. To connect, enter your own OAuth client ID and secret below.'

Architectural intent (per AGENTS.md 'shared core, thin adapters' and 'one token, both protocols'): treat client identity acquisition as multiple pluggable front doors (DCR, CIMD, pre-registered/manual) that all converge on the single existing authorization_code + PKCE core and one HMAC JWT. Fix the OAuth layer once at the mux/middleware level so both /sse (MCP) and /a2a (A2A) benefit; do NOT fork auth per protocol.

This epic is additive, not a rebuild: the OAuth 2.1 + PKCE core (handleTokenExchange, oauth.go:441) and dual-protocol design are sound. Keep CIMD; stop treating it as the exclusive path.

Scope: Priority tasks P1 (RFC 9728 metadata + WWW-Authenticate pointer), P2 (RFC 7591 DCR, coexisting with CIMD), P3 (transport endpoint shape for base-URL probing), and a documentation review/update task covering docs/architecture, docs/dual-protocol-architecture, diagrams, and user guide.

title: P3: Transport endpoint shape for base-URL probing (Streamable HTTP root)
description:
Gemini Spark treats the user-supplied MCP URL as a Streamable-HTTP endpoint and probes the BASE URL: Cloud Logging shows POST / -> 404 and HEAD / -> 404 from User-Agent 'Google' against candir.mithlond.com. The server currently mounts the MCP transport only at /sse (main.go:475), so these base-URL probes miss. This is a transport-shape issue, not OAuth.

WHY: Current MCP clients increasingly expect a single Streamable-HTTP endpoint and will POST/HEAD the given URL directly. If users paste https://candir.mithlond.com/sse the /sse mount is hit, but base-URL probes (and users pasting the bare domain) 404.

WHAT TO DO (decide one, document the decision as an ADR/decision bead if non-trivial):
1. Option A (recommended): also expose the multiplexed MCP handler at a stable base path so POST/HEAD to that path succeed (the existing NewMcpMultiplexerHandler already supports both SSE and Streamable HTTP, main.go:432-433). Ensure it stays behind the same secureHandler chain (oauthMiddleware -> sseLoggingMiddleware -> gate('lexicon:read')).
2. Option B: keep /sse only and make the requirement explicit — document that the URL to paste is https://candir.mithlond.com/sse, and return a helpful, correctly-authenticated response (or documented redirect) for base-URL probes instead of a bare 404.
3. Either way, verify HEAD is handled sanely (not a 404) for the advertised endpoint and that the multiplexer routing (main.go MCP multiplexer) covers the method/paths Spark probes.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Spark's base-URL probes (POST /, HEAD /) no longer dead-end at 404 in a way that blocks connection; behavior is intentional and documented.
- The chosen endpoint remains protected by the existing OAuth + scope gate; no auth bypass introduced.
- Decision recorded (which path, and the exact URL users should paste) and reflected in the user guide (see docs task).

NON-GOALS: OAuth discovery (P1) and DCR (P2).
notes:
DECISION: Option A. Mounted MCP secureHandler at exact base path via mux.Handle("/{$}", secureHandler) in main.go, in addition to /sse. Go 1.25 exact-match pattern '/{$}' matches ONLY '/', so unknown paths still 404.

Behavior (verified locally):
- POST / -> 401 (was 404)
- HEAD / -> 401 (was 404)
- GET / -> 401 with WWW-Authenticate carrying RFC 9728 resource_metadata pointer
- GET /favicon.ico (unknown) -> still 404
- /sse -> unchanged (401 unauth)

Net: Spark's base-URL probes now get a proper auth challenge that also advertises PRM (dovetails with n3l.1), and users may paste EITHER https://candir.mithlond.com OR .../sse — both drive the transport behind the same oauthMiddleware->sseLogging->gate('lexicon:read') chain. No auth bypass. HEAD handled sanely (401, not 404).

Test: TestRootPathMountedForBaseURLProbes (POST/HEAD/GET / -> 401; unknown -> 404). Full suite green, golangci-lint 0 issues. Committed 7771b0e.

title: Phase 3: local OpenAI-compatible backend (llama.cpp + mlx_lm.server) for Gemma 4
description:
Add a new LLM backend implementing skills.LLMClient (from Phase 1) that talks to a local OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint. Two local server runtimes both expose this identical wire protocol and should be supported by the same client code, distinguished only by which base URL/port they're running on:

1. llama.cpp's llama-server, serving GGUF models (user has stock Gemma 4 GGUFs under ~/projects/gemma, and fine-tuned/merged eldamo-gemma GGUFs under ~/projects/eldamo-tune/models/).
2. mlx_lm.server (from the mlx-lm package), serving MLX-format weights with Apple Silicon acceleration. Confirmed via source inspection (mlx_lm/server.py:1106-1107) that it implements /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions with SSE streaming and a standard usage{prompt_tokens,completion_tokens} block (server.py:1339-1341,1567-1569) — i.e. the same shape as llama.cpp's server. User has stock Gemma 4 MLX weights under ~/projects/gemma/mlx-gemma-4-e2b and mlx-gemma-4-e4b, and tuned MLX weights under ~/projects/eldamo-tune/models/mlx, mlx_mobile, mlx_mobile_4b.

Config via generic env vars (not llama.cpp-specific), e.g. LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL (e.g. http://localhost:8080) and LOCAL_LLM_MODEL, since the same client works against either runtime. Follows the self-hiding conditional-registration pattern: if LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL is unset, this backend is simply not selected (mirrors ELVISH_TTS_URL / GEMINI_TRANSLATE_MODEL in a2a.go:80-108).

Note: mlx_lm.generate is NOT a server (one-shot CLI, process exits after generating) — the correct utility is mlx_lm.server.

Per AGENTS.md SSRF rule, outbound requests must go through SafeHTTPClient(), even for a typically-localhost target, since the base URL is operator-configurable and could be pointed elsewhere.
design:
Backend selection precedence should be explicit and documented (e.g. LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL takes precedence over GEMINI_TRANSLATE_MODEL if both set, or vice versa — pick one and document it in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). Parse OpenAI-style streaming SSE chunks (choices[].delta.content) into the same chunk type Phase 1's interface expects — this parsing is identical for llama-server and mlx_lm.server since both implement the same OpenAI wire format. Response usage field (prompt_tokens/completion_tokens) feeds directly into Phase 2's usage tracking with cost=0 (local compute) and a 'runtime' tag (llama.cpp vs mlx) so Phase 2's comparisons can break down local inference by runtime, not just by model.

No separate mlx_lm-specific client code should be needed if the llama.cpp client is written against the OpenAI chat-completions shape generically — verify this assumption early (spike against both a running llama-server and a running mlx_lm.server) before deciding whether one client suffices or two thin variants are warranted.

- New local-OpenAI-compatible backend package/file implementing skills.LLMClient, verified working against BOTH a running llama-server instance and a running mlx_lm.server instance without backend-specific code branches (beyond config).
- LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL / LOCAL_LLM_MODEL env vars documented in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md alongside existing GEMINI_* vars, with a note on llama-server vs mlx_lm.server setup.
- translate and neologism skills work end-to-end against:
  - a local llama-server running a stock Gemma 4 GGUF (~/projects/gemma) and the eldamo-tuned GGUF (~/projects/eldamo-tune/models/eldamo-gemma-q4_k_m.gguf)

  (manually verified by the user)
- Outbound HTTP calls use SafeHTTPClient().
- golangci-lint 0 issues; make test passes.

Caveat: both llama-server and mlx_lm.server load one model per process/port — switching models requires restarting with a different -m/--model, running separate instances on separate ports, or (for llama.cpp) fronting with llama-swap for hot-swap-by-model-name.

Implemented localLLMClient (llm_local.go) — a single skills.LLMClient adapter for the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions streaming protocol shared by llama.cpp's llama-server and mlx-lm's mlx_lm.server. New env vars: LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL (takes precedence over GEMINI_TRANSLATE_MODEL), LOCAL_LLM_MODEL (default 'local-model'), LOCAL_LLM_RUNTIME (usage-tracking tag), LOCAL_LLM_MAX_TOKENS (default 4096). Verified end-to-end against REAL local servers (not just mocks):
- llama-server serving ~/projects/eldamo-tune/models/eldamo-gemma-q4_k_m.gguf (tuned Gemma 4 GGUF): translate + neologism both completed successfully via a2acli.
- mlx_lm.server serving ~/projects/eldamo-tune/models/mlx (tuned Gemma 4 MLX): translate + neologism both completed successfully via a2acli after fixes below.

Real bugs found and fixed during live testing (not caught by mocks alone):
1. Custom dialer picked only ips[0] from LookupIP; 'localhost' resolved to ::1 first but llama-server/mlx_lm.server bind IPv4-only, causing 'connection refused'. Fixed: dialer now tries all resolved IPs in order (Happy-Eyeballs-style fallback).
2. mlx_lm.server treats the request 'model' field as a HF repo ID to load (unlike llama-server, which ignores it) — requires LOCAL_LLM_MODEL=default_model to use the server's --model. Documented prominently in docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
3. Reasoning-enabled Gemma checkpoints stream chain-of-thought via a non-standard 'reasoning' delta field (separate from 'content') on mlx_lm.server; for the skills' large system instructions this can consume the entire max_tokens budget (mlx_lm.server default 512) before any content is produced, yielding empty responses. Fixed by adding configurable max_tokens (default 4096) to requests; documented mlx_lm.server's --chat-template-args '{"enable_thinking":false}' as the practical mitigation (cut generation from minutes to seconds in testing).

title: [EPIC] Support Gemma 4 models for A2A generative skills (llama.cpp + MLX first)
description:
Currently the LLM-backed A2A skills (translate, neologism) are hardcoded to Google's Vertex AI Gemini backend via the google.golang.org/genai SDK (see a2a.go:78-108). There is no pluggable backend abstraction and no way to point at a local or self-hosted model. The user has local Gemma 4 model variants (~/projects/gemma) and a fine-tuned Gemma 4 (~/projects/eldamo-tune/models/) in both GGUF (llama.cpp) and MLX formats, runnable via llama-server or mlx_lm.server (both expose an identical OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions API — confirmed by source inspection of mlx_lm/server.py). The user is also considering a hosted Gemma 4 deployment down the road. Before adding a hosted option, the user wants token/cost usage tracking in place so response quality can be assessed against cost per backend/runtime.

Goal: introduce a pluggable LLM backend abstraction in skills.Deps, add a single local OpenAI-compatible backend that works against both llama-server and mlx_lm.server (same wire protocol, different runtime — useful for comparing llama.cpp vs Apple Silicon MLX-accelerated inference on the same tuned weights), add per-request token/cost usage tracking across all backends, and leave hosted-Gemma as a follow-on decision informed by that usage data.

Mirrors the existing conditional-registration/self-hiding pattern (ELVISH_TTS_URL, GEMINI_TRANSLATE_MODEL) — each backend self-hides when its env config is absent, and skills.Deps.LLMEnabled() gates dispatch in the A2A executor (a2a.go:145,154).
design:
Backend selection is env-var driven and mutually-exclusive-by-default (first configured backend wins), not per-request. All backends implement a small internal LLM client interface (GenerateContent-style) so translate.go/neologism.go stop depending directly on *genai.Client. Because llama-server and mlx_lm.server both speak the same OpenAI-compatible protocol, one client implementation suffices for both — differentiated only by base URL/port and a 'runtime' tag for usage-tracking breakdowns. Token/cost tracking should be backend-agnostic (usage struct: prompt tokens, completion tokens, backend id, runtime id, model id, latency, estimated cost) and logged the same way regardless of backend so Gemini-vs-llama.cpp-vs-mlx-vs-future-hosted-Gemma comparisons are apples-to-apples.

DEVIATION from AGENTS.md's blanket 'use SafeHTTPClient() for all external fetches' rule: the local backend intentionally does NOT reuse SafeHTTPClient() as-is, because that dialer blocks loopback/private IPs to guard against SSRF via arbitrary, per-request, potentially attacker-influenced URLs (CIMD client_id discovery, OAuth redirects). LOCAL_LLM_BASE_URL has a different trust model — a fixed value the operator sets once at process startup (same trust level as GCP_PROJECT/GEMINI_LOCATION), expected to point at localhost/private LAN. A purpose-built localLLMHTTPClient() (llm_local.go) keeps SafeHTTPClient's other protections (resolve-then-dial-to-resolved-IP to avoid DNS-rebinding TOCTOU, bounded redirects, no arbitrary http.Get) but omits the private-IP block, and additionally fixes a latent single-IP-choice bug (tries all resolved IPs in order, since 'localhost' commonly resolves ::1 first but llama-server/mlx_lm.server often bind IPv4-only).

title: agy: simultaneous legacy-SSE + Streamable-HTTP usage causes intermittent 'session not found'
description: agy persistently sends X-Mcp-Force-Sse: true (our own non-standard header, originally added for Antigravity Desktop GFE buffering, see main.go McpMultiplexerHandler) on every request, including GET /sse. This opens a session on the legacy SSE handler, while agy's actual tool-call traffic (POST/DELETE /sse, no session-establishing hint) is correctly routed to the separate Streamable HTTP handler -- two disjoint, non-interoperable session tables for one logical connection. agy also opens redundant duplicate GET /sse streams seconds apart. Confirmed via Cloud Run logs: the failing tools/call POST completes in ~2ms (rejected by the transport layer before reaching tool-execution code) referencing a session ID that was never registered in the Streamable HTTP handler's table. Not fixable server-side -- no MCP server can reconcile one client mixing two transports for a single session. agy's own traffic already works correctly and exclusively via Streamable HTTP whenever this header is absent, so the fix is for agy to stop sending X-Mcp-Force-Sse for this server. Reported to the Antigravity team with full log evidence.

title: agy: double concurrent /api/oauth/token requests on code paste can surface spurious Unauthorized
description: Antigravity's OAuth-code input handler fires two concurrent /api/oauth/token requests ~35-80ms apart when a code is pasted. If the first (malformed/incomplete) request's 400 arrives before the second (valid) request's 200, the client surfaces a spurious 'Unauthorized' and aborts the initialize handshake even though authentication actually succeeded server-side. Confirmed via Cloud Run access logs (byte-size/latency correlation) that the second request does complete successfully. Client-side only; reported to the Antigravity team as a friction report with full log evidence and repro steps. No server-side workaround exists.

title: agy: 'no pending auth state for server <name>' when re-pasting code after failed post-auth initialize
description: Confirmed client-side: correlating exact timestamps against Cloud Run logs shows zero /api/oauth/token network calls at the moment this error appears, meaning agy fails entirely in its own local OAuth state machine before any network I/O. Root chain: code exchange succeeds -> subsequent 'initialize' with the fresh token fails (was our own X-Mcp-Force-Sse bug, now fixed server-side) -> user re-pastes a new code -> agy has already consumed/discarded its one-shot pending-OAuth-state object and never re-arms one for the retry, so the fresh code has nothing to submit against. Reported to the Antigravity team with full log evidence and repro steps. Should occur less often now that the triggering post-auth initialize failure is fixed server-side, but the underlying state-machine bug (no re-arm on connection failure) remains open on agy's side.

Observed: a2acli send 'I need a neologism for the word: chaos...' → routed to name-generate → produced Bessgwaadon (bess+gwae+adu, semantically unrelated to chaos).

title: Reduce log noise: gate debug header dump to invalid tokens, not missing tokens
description:
The [Auth] Debug Headers log line in oauthMiddleware (oauth.go ~line 680) fires on every request that lacks a token entirely, dumping the full header map to Cloud Run stderr. This was added to help diagnose auth rejections but is now generating steady noise from Gemini Spark's OpenAuth library, which fires a bare HEAD /sse probe (no Authorization header) before each conversation turn as a connection health check — a known, expected pattern.

WHAT TO DO:
Gate the debug header dump so it only fires when a token was present but invalid (genuinely suspicious — wrong signature, expired, wrong type claim), NOT when the token is simply absent. The missing-token rejection log line ([Auth] Rejected request HEAD /sse: Missing access token) is sufficient signal for the absent-token case.

Concretely in oauth.go:
- Keep: log.Printf("[Auth] Rejected request %s %s: Missing access token", ...) on the tokenStr == "" path
- Remove or gate behind a higher severity condition: log.Printf("[Auth] Debug Headers for %s %s: %+v", ...) — this should only fire when err != nil on JWT parse (invalid/expired token) or when claims["type"] != "access" (wrong token type)

ACCEPTANCE:
- Spark HEAD /sse probes produce exactly one log line each: [Auth] Rejected request HEAD /sse: Missing access token
- The full header map dump no longer appears for missing-token rejections
- The header dump (or equivalent context) is still emitted when a token IS present but fails signature/expiry/type validation, where it is actually useful for debugging
- golangci-lint 0 issues, go test ./... green
close_reason: Debug header dump moved from missing-token path to invalid-token path (oauth.go). Spark's expected bare HEAD probes now emit one concise log line; header dump only fires when a token is present but fails signature/expiry/claims — where it is actually diagnostic. Committed 96c9b58.

title: [EPIC] eldamo-evaluate: multi-backend response comparison CLI
description:
A standalone CLI tool (cmd/eldamo-evaluate/) for comparing A2A skill response quality and cost across LLM backends and model variants. Separate from eldamo-admin (which is Firebase/Firestore user-management) and separate from a2acli (which is the A2A wire-protocol conformance client). eldamo-evaluate sits on top of both: it orchestrates A2A message/send calls against the running eldamo-server with a fixed prompt set, collects the response text artifacts, correlates with the server's [Usage] log lines (backend, model, prompt/completion tokens, latency, cost_usd emitted by Phase 2), and produces structured output suitable for pasting into docs/model-evaluation.md.

Motivation: now that Phase 2 (eldamo-server-9zq) is live, the token/cost data exists in server logs per call. What's missing is the harness that runs the same fixed prompts across multiple (backend, model) pairs and puts the results side by side. a2acli can send one message; eldamo-evaluate batches the fixed prompt set, captures responses, and formats the comparison.

Scope boundary: eldamo-evaluate is a comparison/research tool, not a conformance tool. A2A protocol correctness (task states, AgentCard, auth) is a2acli's job. eldamo-evaluate's job is: same prompts, different backends, compare output quality + cost. Human evaluation against the fixed prompt set is the right starting point — LLM-as-judge quality scoring is a future phase if warranted.
design: CLI lives in cmd/eldamo-evaluate/ as a standalone Go binary (no Firebase/Firestore dependency). Talks to a running eldamo-server via the A2A JSON-RPC protocol directly (or wraps a2acli as a subprocess — TBD based on which is cleaner for capturing structured output). Config: server URL, JWT token (or AUTH_BYPASS flag for local testing), backend label (for the results table), and a path to the fixed prompt set (YAML/JSON or embedded). Output: a Markdown table row per (prompt, backend) run, ready to paste into docs/model-evaluation.md. Usage log correlation: the server emits [Usage] lines on stderr; eldamo-evaluate should either parse them from a log file/pipe or record them from the response metadata if the A2A task history exposes them.

title: Refactor: reorganise A2A skills into skills/ Go subpackage with injectable index
description:

As skill count grows (name-generate, translate, neologism) and l04.5 brings an injectable taskstore, the right structural moment is to extract skills into a skills/ Go subpackage.   main.go            — bootstrap + mux wiring only

  a2a.go             — dispatcher, card, claimsInterceptor

    translate.go

description:
Longer-term option: deploy a hosted Gemma 4 model (e.g. via Vertex AI Model Garden, GKE, or a managed inference endpoint) as another skills.LLMClient backend, so the A2A translate/neologism skills can run against it instead of Vertex Gemini or local llama.cpp. This is intentionally deferred until Phase 2's token/cost usage tracking has produced enough real data comparing response quality vs cost across the existing Vertex Gemini and local llama.cpp/Gemma backends — the user wants that comparison before committing to hosting infrastructure and its ongoing cost.

Not yet scoped: which hosting mechanism (Model Garden endpoint, GKE + vLLM/llama.cpp server, Cloud Run GPU, etc.) — to be decided once the decision to proceed is made.
design: Should slot into the same skills.LLMClient interface from Phase 1, likely as another OpenAI-compatible or Vertex-endpoint HTTP client depending on hosting choice, reusing Phase 2's usage/cost tracking to fold hosted-Gemma cost into the same comparison table.

title: Consider audio (TTS) artifacts for generated names (Raw/FileURL output)
description:
DISCOVERED via a2acli test-agent capability survey. Eldamo currently returns Text-only artifacts. Since the names/neologisms it generates are Elvish (pronunciation matters), returning a TTS audio rendering as a a2a.NewRawPart(audio/mpeg) or a2a.NewFileURLPart would:
- add genuine utility (hear the name pronounced)
- make eldamo a Raw/URL binary-artifact test target for a2acli (a2ac-mfd)

Exploratory / low priority. Could reuse the genmedia TTS or read-aloud pipeline. Only pursue if pronunciation audio adds real product value.
